stem:
Asha has copper strips, iron strips, a lemon, wires and a small LED.

Which setup is a working Voltaic cell?

options.text: One copper strip and one iron strip in the lemon, connected by wires to the LED.
Two copper strips in the lemon, connected by wires to the LED.
One copper strip and one iron strip in the lemon, connected by wires to the LED — this is a dry cell.
The LED must glow first, and that glow then makes the copper and iron strips in the lemon into a cell.

teacher.key_rationale: A Voltaic cell needs two different metal electrodes in an electrolyte, connected so the LED can glow. Two copper strips omit different materials. Calling the same working setup a dry cell swaps the cell type. Putting LED glow before the cell reverses the causal order.
